name: Titius
overview: Titius Justus was a male worshiper in the city of Corinth whose house was located next to the synagogue. His proximity to the synagogue suggests he was a Gentile believer or God-fearer who showed reverence for the God of Israel. No further tribal or familial details are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Titius Justus is the only recorded name for this individual. There is no specific meaning provided for his name in the biblical text, and it is simply presented as a proper name in Acts 18:7.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Titius Justus beyond what is noted about his worship and residence near the synagogue. There are no additional relational details given.
scriptureSignificance: Titius Justus is significant in the biblical narrative as a worshiper whose house served as a place of Christian fellowship and ministry in Corinth. His willingness to host the apostle Paul or other believers next to the synagogue highlights the early church's outreach to both Jewish and Gentile worshipers. This setting reflects the expansion of the gospel in a key urban center during the apostolic era.
